thread:
alex: Heads-up — found a repeatable long-context mem growth tied to KV cache fragmentation on main canary. After ~2h with many distinct prefixes we see steady RSS growth even though eviction rates look fine. :grimacing:

maya: Can you paste the repro commands and a quick pmap?

alex: repro: run loadgen --seq-len=4096 --unique-prefixes=1e6 --batch=1 --kv-mode=enabled --kv-alloc=slab

alex: pmap snippet (container):
```
00007f9c0000-00007f9c1f000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [anon:kv_cache_buckets]
00007f9c2000-00007f9c2800 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [anon:kv_slab_64]
00007f9c3000-00007f9c3800 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [anon:kv_slab_256]
... repeated many small anonymous mmaps, holes, then big growth in anon:kv_cache_buckets
```

alex: Flamegraph shows lots of time in allocator free/list-manipulation and occasional compaction runs that don't reclaim due to fragmentation.

devon: Do you have allocator stats? free lists per size bin?

alex: yes — snapshot after 2h:
- total_allocated: 18.3GB
- total_committed: 22.9GB
- slab_bins: {64: 48k, 128: 12k, 256: 1.9k, 1024: 430}
- free_frag_ratio: ~0.28 (measured as wasted vs used)

maya: That 64B bin looks suspiciously hot. Tiny objects + long tail of pinned entries -> internal fragmentation.

emily: Did kernel selection or batching changes land around the same time? Could be a correlated regression.

alex: Good call — we rolled batching heuristics v2 last week but kernels unchanged. Profiling shows CPU is the one impacted here (allocator churn), not GPU kernels. Batching actually reduced number of allocations per second, paradoxically making slabs hold longer-lived small entries.

sam: Proposed mitigations?

alex: Two quick experiments I ran:
1) Increase small-block bin size from 64->128 (coalesce allocator frontage). Result: memory peak dropped ~12%, but internal waste up slightly on average allocations. p99 latency +1.5ms, throughput ~same.
2) Opportunistic repack/compaction: background thread takes fragmented slabs with low live density and copies live entries into a fresh slab, frees old one. Ran every 60s with limit 1000 objects. Result: peak down ~18%, CPU overhead +4% during compaction windows. p95 latency bump visible only under sustained compaction.

jordan: Can you share the compaction config snippet?

alex: snippet:
```
kv.compaction.enabled = true
kv.compaction.scan_interval_s = 60
kv.compaction.max_moves_per_run = 1000
kv.compaction.min_live_density = 0.6
kv.compaction.worker_threads = 2
```

devon: Risk: full repack means copying KV entries which may hold pointers into model tensors or attach to caches. Need to ensure we only move lightweight metadata and update references atomically.

alex: We implemented a two-phase move: copy metadata + new pointer to the same KV payload (payload pinned) then swap pointer under per-bucket lock. No tensor duplication. Unit tests added.

emily: Any regression in end-to-end quality (i.e., KV hits/miss behavior)?

alex: No, hit-rate unaffected in tests. We do see slightly higher tail CPU during compaction windows. Also, compaction delays scheduling of low priority background telemetry tasks but that's minor.

sam: Can we combine approaches? i.e., tune bin sizes + occasional compaction for stubborn slabs?

alex: That's what I recommend: smaller compaction frequency + bump 64->96 (empirically 128 helps but increases internal waste). New plan: bump 64->96, compaction every 120s, max_moves 500. That gave ~14% mem reduction in sim.

maya: How about a staging area idea — keep a small hot slab pool that serves new small allocations and periodically drain into normal slabs to avoid creating many semi-live tiny slabs?

alex: I prototyped a 'hot-stage' allocator: short-lived allocations go to a preallocated ring of pages; once ring 70% full we migrate survivors in bulk. This reduced transient fragmentation spikes and smoothed out RSS. Implementation complexity medium.

devon: Sounds promising. Need benchmarks across workloads (long-context chat, high-throughput short queries).

alex: Agreed. I ran two bench suites:
- long-context synthetic: mem peak down 16%, p99 unchanged
- short-queries mixed: mem stable, throughput +0.6%

jordan: What's the rollout plan? Canary flag-prefixed?

alex: Yes — kv_frag_mitigation_v1 as a feature flag. Stage: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> all. Observability: add kv.slab.live_density, kv.compaction.moves, kv.alloc.histogram.

infra-bot: deploy started for canary group "kv-frag-mitigation-v1" on cluster canary-3. (job id: dep-87921) :rocket:

sam: Thanks — once canary metrics look stable let's merge and follow with Dedicated/Private rollout notes. Also add an ops runbook for forced compaction if a node shows runaway RSS.

alex: Will open PR with config, tests, and ops doc. Plan to gather 24h canary metrics and reconvene.

maya: Nice work, Alex. Please add perf graphs to the PR description. :thumbsup:

alex: Will do. Next check-in tomorrow after 24h canary.
